additional_concerns: Candidates node.1bf6918f69c6b37738daeb83, node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e, node.ce439b1cf9ed8301fbb68f94 and node.ea4d19630f8cab09065b1909 turn preserved processing of existing applications into a negative relief condition. Preservation of process supports continued handling under the existing process, but does not expressly establish permanent substantive disqualification of the underlying change. The proposed inference remains unresolved, particularly after a subsequent decision, withdrawal or resubmission.

Candidate node.4d548f2e09bc36ef51212f64 excludes legacy applications from its question and executable scope. That narrower assessment does not resolve their actual eligibility. Candidate node.b66b3e831bb98a12db59dffa similarly assesses substantive conditions only.

The introductory immediate-effect language and the implementation paragraph's specified Effective Date require reconciliation. The date comparison follows the explicit implementation paragraph, but the circular does not fully specify which assessment or implementation event governs every transitional case.

Missing additional authority includes the relevant updated UCITS FAQs and authoritative clarification of the transition's effect on actual relief. The two supplied missing dependency IDs have no identifying descriptions or source hashes, so neither can reliably be assigned to that authority. Applicable home-jurisdiction requirements and any authoritative guidance on novel or complex features and local policy implications are also needed for concrete factual classification.

No separate home-supervision condition should automatically be imported from item (i) into item (ii). The introductory purpose language leaves an interpretive question, but item (ii) expressly uses compliance with home-jurisdiction requirements.

Preservation of the feature exception does not validate each candidate's entire relief rule. None of these predicates establishes legal approval, a complete residual approval obligation, or compliance with separate notification, filing and post-vetting requirements.
